subject: Append data frame(s) to table(s) in remote database

messages.author: 58d4347d38332c5c
messages.subject: Append data frame(s) to table(s) in remote database
parts:
Hi there,

I'm wondering if there is a simple way to append to a remote database using dplyr's framework. For example, suppose I already have the `hflights` table in `my_db`.

library(hflights)
my_db <- src_sqlite("my_db.sqlite3", create = T)
hflights_sqlite <- copy_to(my_db, hflights, temporary = FALSE, indexes = list( c("Year", "Month", "DayofMonth"), "UniqueCarrier", "TailNum"))

Say I want to append the `hflights` data frame to the existing `hflights` table. Is there a simple way to achieve this? If not, may I suggest a new function?

hflights2_sqlite <- append_to(my_db, df=hflights, name="hflights")

By the way, the RMySQL package has an `append` option in the `dbWriteTable` function that does this sort of thing, but I'm trying to make the switch to SQLite ;)


Thanks,

-Carson

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Append data frame(s) to table(s) in remote database
parts:
Hi Carson,

So far, I've steered away from making database modifying functions a
core part of dplyr - copy_to() is mainly there to create test data and
for doing cross-source joins (in which case it creates a temporary
table). Would you mind outlining in a bit more detail why you want
append_to() ?

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Append data frame(s) to table(s) in remote database
parts:
Nevermind. This is actually quite a simple operation and I shouldn't be wasting everyone's time:

library(pitchRx)
dat <- scrape(start = "2013-08-01", end = "2013-08-01")
library(dplyr)
my_db <- src_sqlite("my_db.sqlite3")
dbWriteTable(my_db$con, value = dat$pitch, name = "testing", append = TRUE)
tbl(my_db, "testing")
dbWriteTable(my_db$con, value = dat$pitch, name = "testing", append = TRUE)
tbl(my_db, "testing") #twice as large

-Carson


On Mon, Jan 20, 2014 at 12:04 PM, Carson Sievert <cpsie...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Hadley,

I have an R package which allows me to collect baseball data based on a window of dates.

library(devtools)
install_github('XML2R','cpsievert')
install_github('pitchRx','cpsievert')
library(pitchRx)
dat <- scrape(start = "2013-08-01", end = "2013-08-01")

New data becomes available as more games are played. In the past, I appended new data to existing tables in a MySQL database like so:

library(RMySQL) 
drv <- dbDriver("MySQL") 
MLB <- dbConnect(drv, user="your_user_name", password="your_password", dbname="your_database_name", host="your_host") dbWriteTable(MLB, value = dat$pitch, name = "pitches", append = TRUE)

It would be really nice to have something similar in dplyr for SQLite.

Thanks,

-Carson

modifying database tables could be really interesting and useful.
